cases.prompt: How do I extend the TTL of persistent storage in a Soroban contract?
cases.review: Explains persistent extend_ttl, remaining-ledger thresholds, network limits, and official sources. Discloses conflicting documentation wording.
cases.answer:
Call `env.storage().persistent().extend_ttl(&key, threshold, extend_to)` for each persistent entry you want to extend.

For an existing entry keyed by `DataKey::MyKey`:

```rust
env.storage()
    .persistent()
    .extend_ttl(&DataKey::MyKey, 1000, 5000);
```

This call extends the remaining TTL to **5000 ledgers** when fewer than **1000 ledgers** remain. Otherwise, it changes nothing. Both arguments specify relative ledger counts. See the [official example and tests](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/archival/test-ttl-extension#example).

Call this method after successful reads or writes to keep active entries available. Reads and writes alone do not extend TTL. Each persistent entry has its own TTL. Extensions incur storage rent. See the [storage strategy guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/storage/storage-strategies#strategy-5-ttl-management--bump-on-access).

Choose `extend_to` within the network’s maximum TTL. The [TTL tests](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/archival/test-ttl-extension#example) explain this limit.

Documentation inconsistency: the [dapp guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/dapps/state-archival#1-extending-ttl-from-the-smart-contract) calls these arguments ledger heights. The executable examples and tests show relative ledger counts.

cases.prompt: Which lending protocols are built on Stellar, and which ones got Stellar Community Fund awards?
cases.review: Uses Scout lending discovery and Lumenloop project/submission records. Separates lifecycle status and conflicting award evidence. Official SCF follow-up confirms the joint YieldBlox award amount.
cases.answer:
**Stellar has several lending protocols, and many received Stellar Community Fund (SCF) awards.** The records below reflect Raven’s evidence on October 23, 2026.

The links lead to SCF records unless marked otherwise.

| Protocol | Lending model | Recorded SCF awards |
|---|---|---|
| [Blend](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/blend-mfy) | Customizable lending pools | Liquidity Award, Q1 2024 |
| [Slender](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/slender-t1o) | Lending and borrowing market | #17, #21; Liquidity Award, Q1 2024 |
| [XycLoans](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/xycloans-qqr) | Flash loans | #13; Liquidity Award, Q1 2024 |
| [Alula](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/alula-quk) | Lending with repeated borrowing and deposits | Build #34 |
| [Laina](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rec82ws2Gf1GxiiRZ) | Lending with repeated borrowing and deposits | Build #34 |
| [XOXNO](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/xoxno-new-lending-foundation-protocol-aqo) | Lending pools and flash loans | Build #43 |
| [Peridot Finance](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recAvz5NtVxVvLcMo) | Lending across blockchains | Build #38 |
| [Hatom Protocol](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rec4gKisx5fu7t8nO) | Lending and capital infrastructure | Build #41 |
| [Lucent](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recZeITw6WJDXb0u8) | Stablecoin borrowing against collateral | Build #44 |
| [OrbitCDP](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/orbitcdp-pst) | Stablecoin borrowing against collateral | #21, #25, #29; Liquidity Award, Q2 2025 |
| [FxDAO](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/fxdao-xov) | Stablecoin borrowing against XLM | #13; liquidity awards in 2024 and 2025 |
| [AssetDesk](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/assetdesk-kqx) | Deposits and collateral-backed borrowing | #19 |
| [Mystic](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recqCzftyJOhfSKmB) | Loans against tokenized real-world assets | Activation Award #29 |
| [Lumen Later](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/lumen-later-g5v) | Buy-now-pay-later credit | Build #39 |
| [Legasi](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recJjxMzPmFzSS6v3) | Loans against tokenized assets | Build #40 |
| [YieldBlox](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rec5uH1bD72BKoRPI) | Lending market built on Blend | #7, jointly with OptionBlox |
| [Pluto Loans](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recVYQzThUCdFa0N5) | Loans repaid through future yield | #10, #15 |

Raven also identifies specialized credit and financing projects with SCF awards:

| Project | Focus | Recorded SCF awards |
|---|---|---|
| [Huma](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rectN6ErZmODHk69p) | Payment financing | Activation Award #27 |
| [Microvault](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recvNshb1L59hprMV) | Small loans for farmers | Build #42 |
| [Lendoor](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rec3TJmAPmo6HOPve) | Loans without collateral | Build #45 |
| [HiYield](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recjwQ8Ebg6OIV4BT) | Lending against fixed-income assets | #18 |
| [Liqvid](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recLauVL3boo779AG) | Lending against tokenized assets | Build #37, #45 |
| [Indentura](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recghVchvFzCaKCpO) | Business credit and receivables financing | Build #37 |
| [Airswift / Pelago](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recX7oeV1IsHlgDy5) | Supply-chain financing | #16 |
| [Pipeline](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recBY9t2rdEv609rl) | Commodity trade financing | Build #43 |
| [Trilobyte](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/recq35w2zW5FQu4tY) | Cash-flow financing | #15 |
| [Untangled](https://communityfund.stellar.org/submissions/rec5hF8af5tfhSlT2) | Private-credit assets and investment vaults | Build #31; Liquidity Award, Q3 2025 |

**Other lending protocols have less conclusive award evidence:**

- [K2 Lend](https://stellarlight.xyz/project/k2-lend) offers pooled, isolated, and restricted-access lending markets. Raven’s retrieved records do not confirm an SCF award.
- [Templar Protocol](https://stellarlight.xyz/project/templar-protocol) supports Stellar borrowing through an integration. Raven’s retrieved records do not confirm an SCF award.
- [Polaris Lend](https://stellarlight.xyz/project/polaris-lend) offers fixed-rate, fixed-term lending. Lumenloop lists an SCF #21 award, but Scout disagrees and the submission lookup remains inconclusive.

An award does not establish current availability. Scout marks Slender, OrbitCDP, FxDAO, AssetDesk, Pluto Loans, and Polaris Lend inactive. It marks Laina pre-release and Mystic in development.

Scout also omits award flags for YieldBlox and Pluto Loans. Their linked SCF submission records document historical awards.

cases.prompt: Walk me through adding passkey smart accounts to my Stellar dApp.
cases.review: Reads the smart-account playbook and official documentation. Explains configuration, sign-in, authorization, relayer boundaries, and recovery. Performs no deployment or signing.
cases.answer:
Start on Testnet with **`smart-account-kit`**. Stellar’s current tutorial uses it to create OpenZeppelin smart accounts with passkeys.

Each user gets a contract account. The passkey approves actions, and the account contract checks authorization. A relayer can pay transaction fees. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/contract-accounts/smart-wallets)

1. **Choose the account model.**

   Smart Account Kit supports context rules, multiple signers, and policies such as spending limits.

   `passkey-kit` uses a different account contract with a flat signature map. The two kits are not directly compatible. This walkthrough uses Smart Account Kit. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/contract-accounts/smart-wallets#client-sdks)

2. **Install and configure the browser client.**

   ```bash
   npm install smart-account-kit @stellar/stellar-sdk
   ```

   Create this client only in browser code:

   ```typescript
   import {
     SmartAccountKit,
     IndexedDBStorage,
   } from "smart-account-kit";

   export const account = new SmartAccountKit({
     rpcUrl: "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org",
     networkPassphrase: "Test SDF Network ; September 2015",

     accountWasmHash: "YOUR_ACCOUNT_WASM_HASH",
     webauthnVerifierAddress: "YOUR_WEBAUTHN_VERIFIER_ADDRESS",

     relayerUrl: "/api/send",
     storage: new IndexedDBStorage(),
     rpName: "My Stellar App",
     timeoutInSeconds: 30,
   });
   ```

   Replace both placeholders with values for the selected network. The official tutorial supplies shared Testnet values in its `.env.example`.

   `accountWasmHash` identifies the account contract code. `webauthnVerifierAddress` identifies the contract that checks passkey signatures.

   `IndexedDBStorage` preserves the local session. Create it only in the browser when your application uses server rendering. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/setup-passkeys#the-smart-account-client)

3. **Add fee sponsorship through your server.**

   Get a Testnet relayer key from [OpenZeppelin Channels](https://channels.openzeppelin.com/testnet/gen). Keep the key on your server.

   Implement `POST /api/send` with these steps:

   - Accept either `{ func, auth }` or `{ xdr }`.
   - Reject requests that mix both forms.
   - Forward the payload as `{ params: payload }`.
   - Add `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` on the server.
   - Preserve the relayer’s response status and `{ success, data }` response.

   The kit expects a successful HTTP status and a top-level `success: true`.

   Add request authorization, rate limits, permitted transaction rules, and spending controls before Mainnet. An `Origin` header check alone does not authorize requests. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/setup-passkeys#the-submission-route)

4. **Connect signup, login, and logout.**

   Restore the stored session when the browser application starts:

   ```typescript
   const restored = await account.connectWallet();

   if (!restored) {
     showConnectButton();
   }
   ```

   Run signup from the user’s signup button:

   ```typescript
   const { contractId, submitResult } =
     await account.createWallet("My Stellar App", username, {
       autoSubmit: true,
     });

   if (!submitResult?.success) {
     throw submitResult?.error ?? new Error("Wallet deployment failed");
   }
   ```

   The kit creates a passkey and deploys an account with that passkey as its initial signer.

   Use these calls for login and logout:

   ```typescript
   await account.connectWallet({ prompt: true });
   await account.disconnect();
   ```

   Handle a dismissed passkey prompt without showing a transaction failure. Treat account deployment failure separately from optional Testnet funding failure. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/frontend#user-signup)

   Returning users also need account discovery. The kit uses an indexer to map a credential ID to an account address.

   The documented default uses Mercury’s hosted indexer. Local browser storage does not replace this service. Test login from a fresh browser profile. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/passkeys-prerequisites#finding-a-returning-users-wallet)

5. **Use the account address in contract calls.**

   Your application contract must require authorization from the user’s account address. The guestbook example calls `author.require_auth()`.

   For changes to existing records, require authorization from the stored owner. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/smart-contract#edit_message)

   Build a call with your generated contract bindings. Then pass the assembled transaction to the kit:

   ```typescript
   const transaction = await guestbook.write_message({
     author: contractId,
     title: "Hello",
     text: "Signed with my passkey",
   });

   const result = await account.signAndSubmit(transaction);

   if (!result.success) {
     throw result.error;
   }

   const receipt = await rpc.pollTransaction(result.hash);
   ```

   Here, `guestbook` represents the tutorial’s generated contract client. `rpc` represents your Stellar RPC client.

   The kit handles the passkey prompt, simulation again, and submission. Check the final transaction status before showing success.

   Read any contract return value from the final receipt. Relayer submission returns a transaction hash. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/frontend#sign-the-guestbook)

6. **Test recovery and failure cases before Mainnet.**

   Plan recovery before users deposit assets. Consider a second signer or a recovery policy.

   Test these cases:

   - The user cancels a passkey prompt.
   - The browser has no stored session.
   - The indexer has not found a new account yet.
   - The account no longer accepts the passkey.
   - The relayer rejects a request.
   - Submission succeeds, but the transaction fails.
   - The user loses access to the original passkey.

   The kit checks account creation history, current contract code, and signer ownership before connection. Show a specific message when these checks fail. [Source](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/setup-passkeys#a-few-helpers)

The retrieved repository evidence does not establish complete audit coverage. Its September 1, 2026 note reports no independent audit of the SDK, demo, relayer proxy, or integration code. The underlying contract audit has a separate scope. Review your selected versions and deployed contracts before handling real assets. [Repository](https://github.com/stellar/smart-account-kit)

Source for all asset-to-issuer mappings: [Scout stablecoin registry](https://stellarlight.xyz/api/stablecoins), dated October 23, 2026.

**Three details affect how you use this list:**

- **EURC has two distinct issuers.** Circle and MyKobo issue different Stellar assets with the same code.

cases.prompt: How do I extend the TTL of persistent storage in a Soroban contract?
cases.review: Explains persistent extend_ttl, remaining-ledger thresholds, network limits, and official sources. Discloses conflicting documentation wording.
cases.answer:
Call `env.storage().persistent().extend_ttl(&key, threshold, extend_to)` for each persistent storage entry.

```rust
// Use the key of an existing persistent entry.
env.storage()
    .persistent()
    .extend_ttl(&key, 1000, 5000);
```

This example extends the entry’s TTL to **5000 remaining ledgers** when fewer than **1000 ledgers** remain. Otherwise, the call changes nothing. These values count remaining ledgers, not absolute ledger numbers. See the [official TTL example](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/archival/test-ttl-extension#example).

Call this method after successful reads or writes to keep active entries available. Each persistent entry has its own TTL. Extensions incur rent based on entry size and added ledgers. See the [storage strategy guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/storage/storage-strategies#strategy-5-ttl-management--bump-on-access).

Keep the extension target within the network’s `max_entry_ttl` limit. The network can change this limit.

The [dapp guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/dapps/state-archival#1-extending-ttl-from-the-smart-contract) uses conflicting “ledger height” wording. The TTL example explicitly demonstrates remaining-ledger counts.

cases.prompt: Walk me through adding passkey smart accounts to my Stellar dApp.
cases.review: Reads the smart-account playbook and official documentation. Explains configuration, sign-in, authorization, relayer boundaries, and recovery. Performs no deployment or signing.
cases.answer:
Start with **Smart Account Kit on Testnet**. SDF’s guestbook tutorial uses this path for passkey creation, account deployment, login, and sponsored transactions.

The steps below use documentation retrieved on October 23, 2026.

1. **Choose the account model.**

   A smart account holds assets and checks authorization through `__check_auth`. A passkey lets the user approve actions through WebAuthn.

   Smart Account Kit uses OpenZeppelin accounts with context rules, signers, and policies. Choose it for spending limits or approval thresholds.

   Passkey Kit uses a different signature model. The two kits are not interchangeable. See the [official comparison](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/contract-accounts/smart-wallets#client-sdks).

2. **Install and configure the browser client.**

   ```bash
   npm install smart-account-kit
   ```

   Create one shared client in your browser code:

   ```typescript
   import {
     SmartAccountKit,
     IndexedDBStorage,
   } from "smart-account-kit";

   export const account = new SmartAccountKit({
     rpcUrl: "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org",
     networkPassphrase: "Test SDF Network ; September 2015",
     accountWasmHash: "YOUR_TESTNET_ACCOUNT_WASM_HASH",
     webauthnVerifierAddress: "YOUR_TESTNET_VERIFIER_ADDRESS",
     relayerUrl: "/api/send",
     storage: new IndexedDBStorage(),
     rpName: "My Stellar App",
   });
   ```

   Replace both placeholders with the tutorial’s network configuration. The account hash selects the wallet code. The verifier checks passkey signatures.

   Create `IndexedDBStorage` only in the browser if your app uses server rendering. Follow the [client setup](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/setup-passkeys#the-smart-account-client).

3. **Add a server route for sponsored transactions.**

   The tutorial uses the OpenZeppelin Relayer at `https://channels.openzeppelin.com/testnet`. Obtain a Testnet key through its [key page](https://channels.openzeppelin.com/testnet/gen).

   Keep that key on your server. Configure `/api/send` to:

   - Accept either `{ func, auth }` or `{ xdr }`.
   - Reject requests that mix both formats.
   - Forward the payload as `{ params: ... }`.
   - Add `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` on the server.
   - Preserve the relayer’s response status and `{ success, data }` response.

   Before Mainnet, add request authorization, rate limits, sponsorship limits, and credit monitoring. An origin check alone cannot prevent misuse.

   See the [submission route](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/setup-passkeys#the-submission-route).

4. **Add signup, login, session restore, and logout.**

   Call signup and prompted login from their respective buttons:

   ```typescript
   const created = await account.createWallet(
     "My Stellar App",
     username,
     { autoSubmit: true },
   );

   if (!created.submitResult?.success) {
     throw created.submitResult?.error
       ?? new Error("Account deployment failed");
   }
   ```

   Use these calls for the other actions:

   ```typescript
   // On page load:
   const restored = await account.connectWallet();

   // On the login button:
   await account.connectWallet({ prompt: true });

   // On the logout button:
   await account.disconnect();
   ```

   Signup creates a passkey and deploys a smart account with that passkey as its initial signer.

   Subscribe once to `walletConnected` and `walletDisconnected`. Store the connected `contractId` in your app’s shared state.

   See the [frontend walkthrough](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/frontend#account-type-things).

5. **Connect the account to your contract calls.**

   Pass the smart account’s contract address as the user address. Require authorization for protected actions inside your contract:

   ```rust
   author.require_auth();
   ```

   The [guestbook contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/smart-contract#write_message) demonstrates this check.

   Build your call with generated contract bindings. Then pass the assembled transaction to the account:

   ```typescript
   const result = await account.signAndSubmit(assembledTransaction);

   if (!result.success) {
     throw result.error;
   }

   const receipt = await rpc.pollTransaction(result.hash);
   ```

   `signAndSubmit()` handles passkey approval, repeat simulation, and submission. Check `result.success`; `try/catch` alone does not catch expected submission failures.

   Check the network receipt before showing completion. Read returned contract values from that receipt. See the [transaction example](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/frontend#sign-the-guestbook).

6. **Test returning users and recovery before Mainnet.**

   IndexedDB stores a local session. A separate indexer maps a passkey credential to its account address.

   The default indexer supports discovery from another browser. Disabling discovery prevents login where the browser has no local account record.

   Test page reloads, another browser, cancelled prompts, delayed indexing, failed deployment, and rejected transactions. See the [discovery guidance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/guestbook/passkeys-prerequisites#finding-a-returning-users-wallet).

   Preserve the client’s checks for account creation history, accepted code, and signer ownership. Show specific messages when those checks fail.

   Define and test a lost-passkey recovery process. Verify audit coverage for your exact SDK version and deployed contracts before handling real funds.

Raven can retrieve guidance and explain these steps. Raven cannot sign or submit transactions, change upstream records, or submit applications. Your app and deployment tools perform those actions.

cases.prompt: What does SEP-41 define, and where is its official specification?
cases.review: Retrieves SEP-41 evidence and the official SEP-0041 specification link. Recovers from heading-only documentation results.
cases.answer:
SEP-41 defines the standard token interface for Stellar smart contracts on Soroban. It covers balances, transfers, allowances, burning, metadata, authorization, and events. This common interface lets compatible contracts use tokens consistently. See the [official token interface documentation](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/token-interface).

The official specification is [SEP-0041 in the stellar/stellar-protocol repository](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0041.md).
